description: Thin savoury pancakes of gram flour with onion, tomato and coriander, cooked on the tawa. Ready in twenty minutes.

steps.cue: Smooth and pourable, like thin dosa batter. No lumps.

cues.look: Smooth and pourable, like thin dosa batter, with no lumps.
cues.touch: It runs off the whisk in a steady ribbon.

steps.text: Whisk the besan with turmeric, chilli powder, ajwain, salt and about 250 ml water into a smooth batter. Rest it for 10 minutes.

steps.cue: The vegetables are spread evenly through the batter.

cues.look: The vegetables are spread evenly through the batter.

steps.text: Stir in the finely chopped onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander.

steps.cue: Small bubbles appear and the edges start to lift on their own.

cues.avoid: If the tawa smokes, take it off the flame for a few seconds first, or the chilla sticks and burns.
cues.look: Small bubbles appear and the edges lift on their own.
cues.sound: A gentle sizzle when the batter touches the tawa.

steps.text: Heat the tawa on medium and grease it lightly. Pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread it into a thin circle. Drizzle a little oil around the edge.

steps.cue: Golden-brown spots on both sides and no raw batter in the middle.

cues.look: Golden-brown spots on both sides and no wet batter in the middle.
cues.touch: The middle springs back when pressed with the spatula.

steps.text: Flip and cook the other side, pressing gently. Repeat with the rest of the batter.

title: Besan Chilla

variation_rules.note: Use finely chopped capsicum instead of onion.
Crumble paneer over the chilla before folding for a stuffed chilla.

description: Home-style bone-in chicken in a browned onion and tomato gravy with whole spices. Good with rice or roti.

steps.cue: Every piece is coated in the marinade.

cues.look: Every piece is coated in the marinade.

steps.safety: Wash your hands, the board and the knife with soap after handling raw chicken, and keep raw chicken away from food that will not be cooked. Marinate in the fridge, not on the counter.
steps.text: Mix the chicken with the curd, half the ginger garlic paste, half the turmeric, half the chilli powder and a little salt. Cover and keep in the fridge.

steps.cue: The onions are deep golden brown all over, not black at the edges.

cues.avoid: Don't let the edges go black: the curry turns bitter.
cues.look: The onions are deep golden brown all over.
cues.sound: The sizzle softens as the onions lose their water.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy kadai. Add the whole spices for 30 seconds, then the sliced onions. Cook, stirring more often as they colour.

steps.cue: The tomatoes melt into the masala and oil shines at the edges.

cues.look: The tomatoes melt into the masala and oil shines at the edges.
cues.smell: The raw ginger-garlic smell is gone.
cues.touch: The masala comes away from the pan in one soft mass.

steps.text: Add the rest of the ginger garlic paste for a minute, then the chopped tomatoes, the remaining turmeric and chilli powder, coriander powder and salt. Cook, stirring.

steps.cue: The chicken turns opaque on the outside.

cues.avoid: Keep stirring so the masala doesn't catch on the bottom.
cues.look: Every piece turns opaque on the outside and is coated in masala.
cues.sound: A loud sizzle when the chicken goes in.

steps.text: Add the chicken with all its marinade. Cook on high heat, stirring, so it sears and the masala coats every piece.

steps.cue: The meat pulls away from the bone easily.

cues.look: The gravy bubbles gently, with oil on top.
cues.touch: The meat pulls away from the bone easily; cut the largest piece: no pink inside.

steps.safety: Chicken must be cooked through. Cut the thickest piece open to the bone; the meat should be white with no pink and the juices clear. If unsure, cook 5 more minutes and check again.
steps.text: Add 300 ml hot water, cover and simmer on low heat, stirring now and then.

steps.cue: Fresh garam masala and coriander.
steps.text: Add the garam masala and coriander leaves, cover and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Chicken Curry

variation_rules.note: Kashmiri chilli is mild in heat; halve it for young children.
Pressure-cook for 3 whistles with less water instead of simmering; still check that the chicken is cooked through.

description: Everyday arhar dal, pressure-cooked soft and finished with a ghee tadka of cumin, garlic, onion and tomato.

steps.cue: Soaking is optional but makes the dal cook softer and faster.

cues.look: The rinse water runs almost clear.

steps.text: Rinse the dal 2 to 3 times until the water runs almost clear, then soak in fresh water.

steps.cue: Let the pressure drop by itself. The dal should mash completely when pressed with a spoon.

cues.sound: Count the whistles; then let the pressure drop by itself.
cues.touch: The dal mashes completely when pressed with a spoon.

steps.text: Drain and pressure-cook the dal with 600 ml water and the turmeric on medium heat.

steps.cue: It pours like thick soup and bubbles gently. Stir now and then; dal sticks to the bottom as it thickens.

cues.avoid: Stir now and then; dal sticks to the bottom as it thickens.
cues.look: It pours like thick soup and bubbles gently.

steps.text: Whisk the dal smooth, add the salt and hot water until it pours like thick soup, and simmer.

branch.action: Take out the child's dal before adding the chilli tadka; give it a little ghee and cumin only

steps.cue: Garlic should be golden, not brown. The tomato breaks down and the ghee shines at the edges.

cues.avoid: Don't let the garlic go brown: it turns bitter.
cues.look: Garlic is golden, the tomato has broken down and the ghee shines at the edges.
cues.sound: Cumin crackles as soon as it hits the ghee.

steps.text: For the tadka heat the ghee in a kadai. Add cumin, hing and garlic; when the garlic is golden add onion, ginger and green chilli and cook until the onion is light golden. Add the tomato and chilli powder and cook until soft.

steps.cue: Taste for salt and sourness after the lemon.

cues.taste: Taste for salt and sourness after the lemon.

steps.text: Pour the tadka into the dal, simmer 2 minutes, then add coriander leaves and lemon juice.

title: Dal Tadka

variation_rules.note: A pinch more hing and a little tomato keep the flavour.
Simmer in a covered pot with extra water, stirring, until soft.

description: Spiced Indian scrambled eggs with onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander. Ten minutes, good with pav or roti.

steps.cue: The yolks and whites are fully mixed, a little frothy.

cues.look: The yolks and whites are fully mixed, a little frothy.

steps.text: Beat the eggs with a pinch of the salt.

steps.cue: The tomato breaks down when pressed with the spoon.

cues.look: The onion is soft and see-through, the tomato breaks down when pressed.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai and cook the onion until soft. Add the green chilli and ginger, then the tomato, and cook until the tomato is soft.

steps.cue: The spices smell toasted, not raw. Just 30 seconds: spices burn quickly in a dry pan.

cues.avoid: Just 30 seconds: spices burn quickly in a dry pan.
cues.smell: The spices smell toasted, not raw.

steps.text: Add turmeric, chilli powder, pav bhaji masala and the rest of the salt and stir for 30 seconds.

steps.cue: Soft, moist curds with no runny egg left.

cues.avoid: Don't stop at shiny wet egg: cook until fully set.
cues.look: Soft, moist curds with no runny egg left.
cues.touch: Nothing wet runs out when you press the egg.

steps.safety: Cook until the egg is fully set with no wet or runny parts, especially for children, elders or anyone pregnant.
steps.text: Lower the heat and pour in the eggs. Leave them for 20 seconds, then scramble, scraping the bottom, until fully set.

steps.cue: Steaming hot when served.

cues.look: Steaming hot when served.

steps.text: Add the coriander leaves and serve hot.

title: Egg Bhurji

variation_rules.note: Leave out the chillies for a mild bhurji.

description: Boiled potatoes tossed in a cumin tadka with turmeric, chilli and a squeeze of amchur. Quick, dry and loved by children.

substitutes.note: juice of half a lemon at the end

steps.cue: Let the pressure drop by itself. A knife should slide in easily but the potato should still hold its shape.

cues.sound: Count two whistles, then let the pressure drop by itself.
cues.touch: A knife slides in easily but the potato still holds its shape.

steps.text: Pressure-cook the whole potatoes with water to cover.

steps.cue: Even, bite-sized cubes so they brown together. Cool enough to hold before peeling.

cues.look: Even, bite-sized cubes so they brown together.
cues.touch: Cool enough to hold before peeling.

steps.text: Peel the potatoes once cool enough to touch and cut into bite-sized cubes.

steps.cue: Cumin sizzles and darkens one shade. If it turns black, start again.

cues.avoid: If the cumin turns black, start again: it will taste bitter.
cues.look: Cumin darkens one shade.
cues.sound: The cumin sizzles and crackles straight away.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai. Add cumin, then hing, green chilli and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.

steps.cue: The edges of the potatoes turn golden and slightly crisp.

cues.avoid: Toss gently so the potatoes don't break into mash.
cues.look: The edges turn golden and slightly crisp.
cues.sound: A steady sizzle as you toss.

steps.text: Add turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder, then immediately the potatoes and salt. Toss on medium heat.

steps.cue: Taste one piece for salt and sourness.

cues.taste: Taste one piece for salt and sourness.

steps.text: Sprinkle amchur and coriander leaves, toss once and serve.

title: Jeera Aloo

variation_rules.note: Boil in a covered pot for about 20 minutes until tender.
Leave out the chillies; the cumin and amchur carry the flavour.

description: Tangy curd and besan kadhi simmered slowly, with soft onion pakoras and a ghee tadka of cumin, methi dana and red chilli.

steps.cue: No lumps at all, and as thin as buttermilk.

cues.look: No lumps at all, and as thin as buttermilk.

steps.text: In a big bowl whisk the curd, 6 chammach besan, turmeric, red chilli powder and salt until completely smooth. Add 900 ml water and whisk again.

steps.cue: Keep stirring until the first boil. If you stop, the curd can split.

cues.avoid: Keep stirring until the first boil, or the curd can split.
cues.look: Small bubbles start rising all over.

steps.text: Pour into the kadai with the grated ginger. Bring to a boil on medium heat, stirring all the time.

steps.cue: It thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon, and the raw besan smell is gone.

cues.look: It coats the back of a spoon.
cues.smell: The raw besan smell is gone.

steps.text: Lower the heat and let the kadhi simmer, stirring every few minutes.

steps.cue: Thick enough to drop from a spoon in a blob. A drop of batter floats in a bowl of water.

cues.look: A drop of batter floats in a bowl of water.
cues.touch: Thick enough to drop from a spoon in a blob.

steps.text: Meanwhile make the pakora batter. Mix 2 katori besan with the sliced onion, green chilli, ajwain, a little salt and the soda, adding about 100 ml water slowly. Beat for 2 minutes.

steps.cue: The pakoras rise to the top and turn golden in about 4 minutes per batch.

cues.avoid: If the oil smokes, turn it down: the outside browns before the inside cooks.
cues.look: The pakoras rise to the top and turn golden all over.
cues.sound: Fast, steady bubbling around each pakora; it quietens as they cook through.

steps.safety: Keep children away from the hot oil. Slide the batter in close to the oil so it does not splash, and never let water drip into hot oil.
steps.text: Heat the oil in a second pan on medium. Drop small spoonfuls of batter and fry in batches until golden all over.

steps.cue: The pakoras turn soft and soak up the kadhi.

cues.touch: The pakoras turn soft and soak up the kadhi.

steps.text: Add the pakoras to the kadhi and simmer for 5 more minutes so they soak it up.

branch.action: Take out the child's portion before pouring the chilli tadka

steps.cue: Cumin darkens one shade in a few seconds. Add the chilli powder off the heat so it turns red, not black.

cues.avoid: Add the chilli powder off the heat so it turns red, not black.
cues.look: Cumin darkens one shade in a few seconds; the chilli powder turns red.
cues.sound: A loud sizzle as the tadka hits the kadhi.

steps.text: For the tadka, heat the ghee. Add cumin, methi dana, dry red chillies and hing. Turn off the heat, add Kashmiri chilli powder and pour over the kadhi at once.

title: Kadhi Pakora

variation_rules.note: Use about 1.2 litres chaas and skip the extra water.
Plain kadhi without pakoras is ready in about 30 minutes.
Make the pakoras with a little chopped methi or plain besan instead of onion.

description: Flattened rice tossed with onion, mustard seeds, curry leaves and crunchy peanuts, finished with lemon and coriander.

steps.cue: A flake pressed between two fingers mashes easily but the poha is not mushy or wet.

cues.avoid: Don't soak it: wet poha turns into a lump.
cues.touch: A flake pressed between two fingers mashes easily but isn't mushy or wet.

steps.text: Put the poha in a sieve and rinse under running water for a few seconds, 2 to 3 times. Do not soak. Sprinkle turmeric, salt and sugar, toss gently and leave for 5 minutes.

steps.cue: The peanuts turn a shade darker and smell roasted.

cues.look: The peanuts turn one shade darker.
cues.smell: Roasted, like a street-side mungfali cart.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai and fry the peanuts until crunchy. Lift them out.

steps.cue: The onion turns translucent, not brown.

cues.look: The onion turns translucent, not brown.
cues.smell: Curry leaves smell fresh and sharp when they hit the oil.
cues.sound: Mustard seeds pop; wait for the popping before adding the rest.

steps.text: In the same oil add mustard seeds. When they pop, add curry leaves and green chilli, then the onion. Cook until soft.

steps.cue: The poha is hot all the way through and every flake is yellow.

cues.look: Every flake is yellow and steam rises when you lift the lid.

steps.text: Add the poha and toss gently on low heat. Cover and steam for 2 minutes.

steps.cue: Taste for lemon and salt.
steps.text: Turn off the heat. Add the peanuts, lemon juice and coriander leaves and toss once.

title: Kanda Poha

variation_rules.note: Leave out the peanuts; add a handful of roasted chana dal or none.
Add one small diced potato with the onion and cook covered until soft for batata poha.

description: Soft paneer and green peas in an onion-tomato gravy with Kashmiri chilli, finished with kasuri methi.

substitutes.note: firm tofu; add it at the very end

steps.cue: The paneer stays soft in the warm water.

cues.touch: The paneer stays soft in the warm water.

steps.text: Cut the paneer into cubes and soak them in warm water so they stay soft. Grind the onion, ginger, garlic and green chilli to a paste, and the tomatoes to a separate puree.

steps.cue: The raw onion smell goes and the paste turns golden.

cues.avoid: Stir often; onion paste catches on the bottom quickly.
cues.look: The paste turns golden.
cues.smell: The raw onion smell goes away.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai. Add cumin and the bay leaf, then the onion paste. Cook, stirring.

steps.cue: The masala thickens, darkens and the oil separates at the edges.

cues.look: The masala thickens, darkens and the oil separates at the edges.
cues.sound: The masala splutters less as the water cooks off.

steps.text: Add turmeric, Kashmiri chilli and coriander powder with a splash of water, stir for a minute, then add the tomato puree. Keep cooking and stirring.

steps.cue: Fresh peas take about 8 minutes; frozen peas about 4.

cues.touch: A pea squashes easily between two fingers.

steps.text: Add the peas, salt and 300 ml water. Cover and simmer until the peas are soft.

steps.cue: Do not boil the paneer for long or it turns rubbery.

cues.avoid: Don't boil the paneer for long or it turns rubbery.
cues.touch: The paneer is soft when pressed with a spoon.

steps.text: Drain the paneer and add it to the gravy. Simmer for 3 minutes only.

steps.cue: Kasuri methi smells sweet and grassy.

cues.smell: Kasuri methi smells sweet and grassy.

steps.text: Add garam masala, crushed kasuri methi and cream. Stir, top with coriander leaves and serve.

title: Matar Paneer

variation_rules.note: Firm tofu and no cream.
A tomato-only gravy with hing; add a little cashew paste for body.

description: Soft rice and yellow moong dal cooked together with ghee, cumin and ginger. Light, one-pot and easy on the stomach.

steps.cue: The rinse water runs almost clear.

cues.look: The rinse water runs almost clear.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and dal together 2 to 3 times and soak them in fresh water.

steps.cue: The cumin sizzles and smells toasty.

cues.avoid: Thirty seconds is enough; don't let the ginger brown.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in the pressure cooker. Add cumin, hing and grated ginger and stir for 30 seconds.

branch.action: Add another half cup of water for a softer khichdi

steps.cue: Let the pressure drop by itself before opening.

cues.sound: Count the whistles, then let the pressure drop by itself before opening.

steps.text: Add the drained rice and dal, turmeric, salt and 900 ml water. Close the lid and cook on medium heat.

steps.cue: It should flow slowly from the spoon, like a thick porridge. It thickens as it stands.

cues.look: It flows slowly from the spoon, like a thick porridge.
cues.touch: The rice and dal mash easily together.

steps.text: Stir and mash lightly. Add hot water if it is too thick, and serve with a little ghee on top.

title: Moong Dal Khichdi

variation_rules.note: Leave out the ginger; the hing and cumin are enough.
Use oil instead of ghee.

description: Kidney beans soaked overnight, pressure-cooked until creamy and simmered in a thick onion-tomato masala. Best with steamed rice.

steps.cue: The beans double in size and the skins are smooth.

cues.look: The beans double in size and the skins are smooth.

steps.text: Rinse the rajma and soak in plenty of water overnight, at least 8 hours.

steps.cue: Let the pressure drop by itself. A bean should mash easily between two fingers and be creamy inside.

cues.sound: Count the whistles, then let the pressure drop by itself.
cues.touch: A bean mashes easily between two fingers and is creamy inside.

steps.safety: Raw or undercooked kidney beans are poisonous. Always soak, throw away the soaking water, and cook until every bean is completely soft. If any bean is still firm, cook for more whistles. Never cook rajma from raw in a slow cooker.
steps.text: Drain and throw away the soaking water. Pressure-cook the rajma with 750 ml fresh water and the salt.

steps.cue: The onion is evenly golden brown at the edges.

cues.avoid: Don't rush on high heat: the edges burn before the middle cooks.
cues.look: The onion is evenly golden brown.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai. Add cumin and the bay leaf, then the finely chopped onion and cook until deep golden.

steps.cue: The masala is thick and dark and the oil leaves the sides.

cues.look: The masala is thick and dark and the oil leaves the sides.
cues.smell: The raw tomato smell is gone.

steps.text: Add grated ginger, garlic and green chilli for a minute, then the tomato puree, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli and coriander powder. Cook, stirring.

steps.cue: The gravy thickens and coats the beans.

cues.avoid: Stir from the bottom every few minutes; rajma gravy sticks.
cues.look: The gravy thickens and coats the beans.

steps.text: Add the rajma with its cooking water. Mash a few beans against the side of the pan for body and simmer on low heat.

steps.cue: Fresh garam masala and coriander.
steps.text: Add garam masala and coriander leaves and serve with rice.

title: Rajma

variation_rules.note: Boil hard for the first 10 minutes, then simmer covered until every bean is completely soft.
Only quick if the rajma is already soaked or boiled.
